findings.problem: A critic answer that is malformed twice is stored as {verdict: PASS, issues: [], attempt} and cannot be told apart from a real PASS in criticReports or model_call. That includes an explicit {"verdict":"FAIL","issues":[]}. The spec allows this (scenario-reasoning.md FR-22 Rules and the slice 10 critic(a) section, contract-notes #15 'to confirm at approval'), and the Evidence Guard is still the hard gate, so it is not a safety hole: a prompt injection in the pack could just as easily make the critic return a well-formed PASS. The cost is audit only: a skipped critic leaves just the WARN log line.
findings.fix: Confirm at approval. If an audit trail is wanted later, add a marker (for example a `degraded` flag or a dedicated reason) to the stored report. No code change for this slice.

findings.problem: normalize() removes \p{Cc}, \p{Zl}, \p{Zp} and ASCII \s. Java's \s and String.trim() do not cover U+00A0 / U+2007 / U+202F or format characters (\p{Cf}, such as bidi overrides U+202E and zero-width spaces). So a description made only of NBSP or zero-width characters passes the 'must not be blank' rule, and bidi controls reach the UI text. Angular interpolation keeps this safe from XSS, but the result can be an empty-looking or visually reordered critic note.
findings.fix: Also map \p{Z} and \p{Cf} to a space (or use strip() plus the UNICODE_CHARACTER_CLASS flag) before the blank check.

findings.problem: The spec (UI section of slice 10) names the component input `openCriticIssues`. The implementation keeps the older input name `issues`. Behaviour and data-testids match the spec.
findings.fix: Rename the input to openCriticIssues (and update the binding in future-result.ts), or align the spec wording.

findings.problem: The description says GenerationRun.hasOpenCriticIssues is 'always sent by the backend from slice 10 on', but the field is not in the schema's `required` list. As a result the generated frontend type stays optional.
findings.fix: Add hasOpenCriticIssues to GenerationRun.required (the backend already always sets it).

findings.problem: The critic adds up to 4 calls per run (2 critiqued attempts, each with a malformed retry). With oracul.openai.timeout PT30S and one transport retry per call, the worst case of the whole pipeline is far beyond the 180 s deadline. The RunGuard check in beforeSend and lockAndCheck on every commit end such runs cleanly (failTimedOut), and nothing is left half-written. The critic is never skipped based on the time left, so a slow but healthy ChatGPT may time out a run that would otherwise have completed.
findings.fix: No change required by the spec. Optionally skip a second critic, or its malformed retry, when the time left before deadline_at is less than one call timeout.
